cohort: Participants were pregnant women attending the department of obstetrics and gynaecology at Kodagu Institute of Medical Sciences (KOIMS), Madikeri, between February 2024 and February 2025.
finding: While maternal complications were not statistically associated with elevated BMI, neonatal outcomes such as low Apgar scores at 1 minute and fetal macrosomia showed significant correlations with maternal overweight and obesity.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was the most common mode of delivery, primarily due to previous cesarean sections, but showed no statistically significant association with elevated maternal BMI.
birth_weight: 82.5% of neonates weighed 2.5-3.99 kg, while low birth weight (<2.5 kg) and macrosomic (>=4 kg) infants each accounted for 8.8%.
gest_age: Most participants presented and delivered at term gestation (37-40 weeks).
